functions.higher_is_better: Shortfall grows as the value falls below the target floor: level_pct = (target − value) ⁄ scale × 100. scale defaults to |target|.
functions.lower_is_better: Overshoot grows as the value rises above the target ceiling: level_pct = (value − target) ⁄ scale × 100. scale defaults to |target|; scale is required when target = 0.
functions.band: Safe inside [low, high]; distance outside the band relative to its width: below → (low − value) ⁄ (high − low) × 100, above → (value − high) ⁄ (high − low) × 100, inside → negative distance to the nearer edge relative to width.

food.food-insecurity-rate.rationale: Best-performing US counties hold overall food insecurity near 5% (Feeding America Map the Meal Gap); treating that as the local floor of what is achievable.

health.uninsured-rate.rationale: States with near-universal coverage programs reach ~3–5% uninsured among under-65s (KFF); 5% marks the boundary of adequate access.

health.life-expectancy.rationale: 80 years approximates the current OECD frontier and top-quartile US county performance (CDC/NCHS USALEEP).

education.hs-attainment.rationale: 95% adult secondary attainment is the practical ceiling observed in high-performing US metros (ACS S1501); below it, attainment gaps concentrate in marginalized groups.

income-work.poverty-rate.rationale: 8% is roughly the floor achieved by US metros with strong labor markets and safety nets (ACS S1701); below-target performance indicates broadly shared income security.

income-work.unemployment-rate.rationale: 4% approximates full employment in the US labor-market literature (CBO natural rate estimates).

water-sanitation.safe-drinking-water.rationale: Safe drinking water is a binary right: any population served by a system in health-based violation (EPA SDWIS) is a shortfall.

energy.energy-burden.rationale: Energy burden above 6% of income is the standard affordability threshold in DOE/ACEEE burden studies.

networks.broadband-access.rationale: 95% household subscription is the level at which broadband functions as universal infrastructure (ACS S2801 top performers; FCC universal-service goal).

housing.cost-burdened-renters.rationale: The 30%-of-income standard defines cost burden (HUD); a healthy market keeps the share of burdened renter households at or below ~30% (pre-2000 US norm).

housing.homelessness-rate.rationale: 10 per 10,000 approximates the rate in US communities that have reached functional zero for major subpopulations (HUD PIT counts); the goal is zero, but 10/10k marks the boundary between crisis and managed response.

gender-equality.gender-pay-ratio.rationale: Median-earnings parity within 5% (ACS S2002) is the observed frontier after occupational-mix effects; the aspiration is 100%.

social-equity.gini-index.rationale: Gini above 0.40 is the conventional warning level for social cohesion (UN-Habitat); most equitable US metros sit near 0.40 (ACS B19083).

political-voice.voter-turnout.rationale: 70% registered-voter turnout in general elections matches high-participation US states and OECD democracies.

peace-justice.violent-crime-rate.rationale: 4 per 1,000 approximates the violent-crime rate of the safest quartile of US cities (FBI UCR/NIBRS).

climate-change.ghg-per-capita.rationale: ~2.5 tCO2e per person per year is the 2030 waypoint on a 1.5°C-compatible per-capita pathway (IPCC AR6 / C40 headline target).

ocean-acidification.aragonite-saturation.rationale: Ω aragonite ≥ 3 supports shell-forming organisms; below ~3 coastal ecosystems show stress, and Ω 1 is dissolution (planetary-boundary literature, Feely et al.).

chemical-pollution.tri-releases-per-capi.rationale: 1 lb per resident per year of TRI on-site releases approximates the best-quartile of US counties with reporting industry (EPA TRI); zero is the aspiration.

nitrogen-phosphorus-loading.nitrate-grou.rationale: 5 mg/L NO3-N is half the EPA MCL (10 mg/L) and the level at which ecological effects and treatment costs begin; background levels are <1 mg/L.

freshwater-withdrawals.residential-gpcd.rationale: 55 gallons per capita per day is California's indoor residential efficiency standard (AB 1668), a defensible sustainable-use benchmark for western US municipalities.

land-conversion.natural-land-conversion.rationale: Holding natural-land loss below 0.5% per decade approximates no-net-loss once restoration is counted; sustained faster conversion is incompatible with local ecological integrity.

biodiversity-loss.protected-land-share.rationale: 30% durably protected by 2030 is the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework target, downscaled directly to the jurisdiction.

air-pollution.pm25-annual.rationale: 5 µg/m³ annual mean is the WHO 2021 air-quality guideline; the US NAAQS (9 µg/m³) is a regulatory floor, not a health-based target.

extreme-heat.hvi-high-share.rationale: Share of residents living in the two highest classes of the jurisdiction's adopted heat-vulnerability index (e.g. NYC DOHMH HVI 4-5). Where a heat-vulnerability instrument exists it is the government's own statement of who heat endangers, and eliminating high vulnerability is the adopted direction of travel — so the boundary is zero share in the highest classes.

extreme-heat.heat-mortality-per-100k.rationale: Heat-attributable deaths per 100,000 residents per year, from the health department's heat mortality reporting. Zero is the only defensible ceiling for a preventable-death hazard (Vision-Zero style); scored as distance from zero against a large-US-city baseline of ~6 per 100k (NYC 2014-2023 average ≈ 5.9). Override the scale per tenant where a local baseline is published.
